accepted.s: An Eco-sensitive Zone (ESZ) around a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary is best understood as a
o: shock absorber and transition zone between high protection and areas where some development may be allowed
strictly urbanised buffer for industrial development
zone where all forms of human activity are permanently prohibited
separate category of biosphere reserve administered by UNESCO
accepted.x: An ESZ functions as a shock absorber around a protected area, providing a transition from high protection to areas where regulated development may be permitted.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the transition-zone concept from absolute protection and unrestricted development.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Eco-sensitive Zones are notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under the
accepted.x: ESZs are notified by MoEF&CC under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and not under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method and distinguish the governing statute from the protected-area statute.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Eco-sensitive Zones:

1. They are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. Their legal basis includes Section 3 read with Rule 5 of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986.
3. They are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because ESZs are not notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong governing-law statement; the statute swap is the key trap.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2011 guidelines of the Ministry of Environment permit an Eco-sensitive Zone extending up to
accepted.x: The 2011 MoEF guidelines allow an ESZ of up to 10 kilometres around a protected area.
accepted.tq: Separate the guideline distance from the later Supreme Court minimum mining buffer.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the Supreme Court position on mining around National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries?
o: Mining is prohibited within exactly 10 kilometres of every protected area in all circumstances.
Mining is impermissible within 1 kilometre of every National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, unless a larger ESZ is notified; the larger buffer then applies.
Mining is permitted within 1 kilometre if the State Government approves it.
Mining is prohibited only inside National Parks and is permitted around Wildlife Sanctuaries.
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held that mining is impermissible within 1 kilometre of every National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary; where a larger ESZ is notified, the larger buffer prevails. Mining inside the protected area is also barred under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory prohibition inside the protected area from the judicial minimum buffer outside it.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Projects affecting wildlife in or around protected areas require clearance from the
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
accepted.x: Projects affecting wildlife require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).
accepted.tq: Identify the authority by matching the function—wildlife project clearance—with the competent statutory body.

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is classified as PROHIBITED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
accepted.x: Commercial mining and quarrying are prohibited activities in ESZs. Ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted activities.
accepted.tq: Classify the activity under the prohibited–regulated–permitted framework.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only activities classified as REGULATED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
o: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening
Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting
Major hydro projects, commercial mining, ongoing agriculture
accepted.x: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, and road widening are regulated activities. Commercial mining and major hydro projects are prohibited, while ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.
accepted.tq: Use category elimination by checking whether each activity belongs to the same regulatory class.
accepted.sec: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is classified as PERMITTED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
accepted.x: Rainwater harvesting is a permitted activity in an ESZ. Major hydro projects, polluting industries and commercial quarrying are prohibited.
accepted.tq: Use the permitted-category examples to reject activities from the prohibited list.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, consider the following statements:

1. The relevant Supreme Court ruling was in A. John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu.
2. The ruling was delivered in 2025.
3. Tamil Nadu subsequently issued eviction notices for forest land inside the reserve.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Following the 2025 ruling in A. John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu, Tamil Nadu issued eviction notices concerning forest land inside the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.
accepted.tq: Combine the case name, year and administrative consequence without confusing the court order with ESZ notification powers.
